text: Operate package follows. First, load package. example, demonstrate package can tackle urban-scale climate risk robust infrastructure assessment geospatial planning. run demo_data_load() function load set demo datasets run package’s function. demo data contains coordinate-point location public drinking water fountains city Naples, Italy, well gridded population raster data GHS-POP, 100-m resolution map heat hazard (number days Wet-Bulb Globe Temperature greater 25° C historical period 2008-2017, obtained UrbClim model), administrative boundaries city.  , can use traveltime function generate map current accessibility facility point sf input (, fountains) within specified geographical boundaries, choosen travel mode (walk fastest), given output spatial resolution (meters; achieved using disseving spatial downscaling techniques). function run successfully, can generate map resulting layer using traveltime_plot function.  can also produce summary plot statistic based output traveltime function given demand (e.g., population) raster, well given time threshold parameter: print summary cumulative curve plot output message : can now use allocation function optmise spatial allocation new water fountains ensure (virtually) everyone (.e., totality raster layer specified demand_raster parameter) can walk one within 15 minutes, specified objectiveminutes parameter:  Note also possible solve allocation problem specifying weights parameter, attribute relative importance priority areas demand_raster overlapping weighting factors (defined another raster layer), exposure hot days, following example:  also possible define different demand weighting layers normalisation exponentiation (increase relative role two respect one another) via approach, exp_demand, exp_weights parameters (see package helpfile details): variant allocation problem case set candidate locations allocate new faciltiies discrete (continuous study area, previous example). case, user needs provide discrete set location points candidate parameter allocation_discrete function, well maximum number facilities (n_fac parameter) can selected among candidate locations. function apply quasi-optimality heuristic (using randomisation based approach, number replications - defined n_samples parameters - gradually approach global optimum linearly increase computational time.  Consider also case problem existing facilities start , hence discrete location-allocation problem needs optimise allocation cover much possible demand within limited set discrete choices space allocate new facilities, well constraint set maximum number allocable facilities:  course, also case discrete allocation problem, weight layer weights normalisation exponentiation parameters can set arguments function.
code: library(locationallocation) demo_data_load()  out_tt <- traveltime(facilities=fountains, bb_area=boundary, dowscaling_model_type="lm", mode="walk", res_output=100)  traveltime_plot(traveltime=out_tt,  bb_area=boundary, facilities = fountains) traveltime_stats(traveltime = out_tt, demand_raster = pop, breaks=c(5, 10, 15, 30), objectiveminutes=5) [1] "38.54 % of demand layer within the objectiveminutes threshold." output_allocation <- allocation(demand_raster = pop, traveltime_raster=out_tt, bb_area = boundary, facilities=fountains, weights=NULL, objectiveminutes=15, objectiveshare=0.99, heur="max", dowscaling_model_type="lm", mode="walk", res_output=100)  allocation_plot(output_allocation, bb_area = boundary) output_allocation_weighted <- allocation(demand_raster = pop, traveltime_raster=out_tt, bb_area = boundary, facilities=fountains, weights=hotdays, objectiveminutes=15, objectiveshare=0.99, heur="max", dowscaling_model_type="lm", mode="walk", res_output=100)  allocation_plot(output_allocation_weighted, bb_area = boundary) output_allocation_weighted_2 <- allocation(demand_raster = pop, traveltime_raster=out_tt, bb_area = boundary, facilities=fountains, weights=hotdays, objectiveminutes=15, objectiveshare=0.99, heur="max", dowscaling_model_type="lm", mode="walk", res_output=100, approach = "norm", exp_demand = 2, exp_weights = 1) candidates <- st_sample(boundary, 300)  output_allocation_discrete <- allocation_discrete(demand_raster = pop, traveltime_raster=NULL, bb_area = boundary, facilities=fountains, candidate=candidates, n_fac = 10, weights=NULL, objectiveminutes=15, dowscaling_model_type="lm", mode="walk", res_output=100, n_samples=1000)  allocation_plot_discrete(output_allocation_discrete, bb_area = boundary) set.seed(333)  output_allocation_discrete_from_scratch <- allocation_discrete(demand_raster = pop, traveltime_raster=NULL, bb_area = boundary, facilities=NULL, candidate=candidates, n_fac = 10, weights=NULL, objectiveminutes=15, dowscaling_model_type="lm", mode="walk", res_output=100, n_samples=1000)  allocation_plot_discrete(output_allocation_discrete_from_scratch, bb_area = boundary)
